result.title: VisHead-Spec: Head-Routed Visual Attention for Multimodal Speculative Decoding
result.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates vision-language models(VLMs) while preserving the target model's outputs, but its speedup diminishes under high concurrency serving as the system becomes more compute bounded as the batch size increases. This problem is pronounced for multimodal speculative decoding as the long range of the image tokens in the prompt can significantly increase the computational cost during draft token prediction. The block-diffusion drafters (e.g. DFlash, DSpark) can effectively speed up the draft model efficiency by predicting multiple draft tokens in one forward pass, but their speedup for VLMs under high concurrency is still modest (<9%). In order to understand this gap, we examine the information flow between different modalities from target model to draft model and identify the sparsity pattern of visual attention between the target and draft models: only small set of key-value heads in the draft model need direct visual feature attention in the context and only visual features from top level layers in the target model need to be attended in the context. We therefore propose VisHead-Spec, which selects a small, fixed set of key-value (KV) heads to attend to all image features from top level layers in the target model and restricts the remaining heads to text features. On Qwen3-VL-8B and MMSpec, VisHead-Spec-8 lets 8 of the drafter's 40 KV heads read the image while keeping accepted length within 0.3% of the block-diffusion draft model baseline (i.e. DSpark). At batch size 64, its throughput gain over autoregressive decoding increases to 16.0%, compared with 9.5% for DSpark; at batch size 1, its speedup remains comparable to DSpark.

AI.brief_summary: 该文面向高并发下的多模态投机解码，分析 target 模型到 draft 模型的信息流，发现仅少数 KV 头需要直接读取 target 顶层视觉特征，据此设计固定少量 KV 头路由图像、其余头只看文本的 VisHead-Spec，在保持接受长度基本不变的同时提升吞吐。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉信息只由少数 KV 头承载、且集中在 target 高层」的稀疏路由观察，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据在内部状态中的分布、视觉旁路与信息坍缩诊断提供可供核查的线索，但论文目标是解码加速而非推理机制本身。
